news.title: AkzoNobel doet tóch zaken met Nippon Paint
AkzoNobel heeft zijn activiteiten op het gebied van decoratieve verven in Zuidoost-Azië verkocht aan Nippon Paint voor 1,35 miljard dollar.

summary: AkzoNobel is dutch chemical company, founded in 1994. Type: listed company. About 35,200 employees (Wikidata). Revenue Q4916 10.7 billion (2023). insights.one_liner: AkzoNobel is the Amsterdam-based paints and coatings giant behind Dulux and Sikkens, currently selling businesses while it prepares a merger with Axalta.

culture.text: A big corporate: around 34,000 people in 150+ countries according to its website, with headquarters in Amsterdam.
Staff on LinkedIn mostly studied business, chemistry, marketing or chemical engineering, with VU Amsterdam among the top schools.
Its 2 open jobs here are both internships, in Amsterdam and Sassenheim, in product management and research.

open.text: AkzoNobel is not listed in the IND register of recognised sponsors under this name.
Both current postings need no Dutch and one mentions visa or relocation.
It is active in more than 150 countries and says it wants a diverse team.

growth.text: Staff fell slightly from 35,700 in 2017 to 35,200 in 2023.
In 2023 it made €10.668 billion in revenue and €488 million net profit.
It sold its decorative paints business in Southeast Asia to Nippon Paint for €1.2 billion.

worth_knowing.text: AkzoNobel is preparing a merger with American coatings maker Axalta, which could reshape teams and roles.
The Asia paint sale came just before the merger, so the company is shrinking its footprint in some regions.
